problemStatement.formal: Given a random walk in Z^2 starting at the origin, let F(k) = {x : f_k(x) = max_y f_k(y)} be the set of most-visited points at step k. Is |union_{k <= n} F(k)| <= (log n)^{O(1)} almost surely?
problemStatement.plain: For a random walk in Z^2, the cumulative set of most-visited points through step n grows at most polylogarithmically. Specifically, |union_{k <= n} F(k)| = O((log n)^2) almost surely.
